newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 24.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
-- COMPAQ BUYS TANDEM FOR $3 BILLION

Personal computer company Compaq is to acquire Tandem Computers Inc, a California-based manufacturer of high performance mainframe computers, in a stock-swap deal valued at about $3 billion (1.8 billion stg). Compaq, the world's leading supplier of PCs, has set itself a target of more than doubling its revenues to $40 billion by the year 2000. The Tandem deal could accelerate Compaq's growth to the extent that it replaces IBM as the world's leading computer manufacturer by the turn of the century.
-- TOP FOOTBALL CLUBS CONSIDER PAY-TV LAUNCH

A report commissioned by soccer's Premier League has recommended that it establish its own television network when its current deal with BSkyB, the satellite broadcaster, expires in 2001. Media consultants Oliver & Ohlbaum delivered the report to the League two weeks ago. It claimed that the 670 million stg that BSkyB is paying to screen live games over the next four years is only half the real value of the rights.
-- WH SMITH CHIEF QUITS TO JOIN BT AFTER 18 MONTHS

Bill Cockburn, chief executive of high street retailer WH Smith Group Plc, is to leave the post to become managing director of British Telecommunications Plc. The surprise departure, after just 18 months at WH Smith, sent shares in the group tumbling to a two-year low. Cockburn had joined Smiths with a brief to revitalise the chain of WH Smith stores in the face of competition from specialist retailers and supermarkets. The move will raise concerns as to the potential for recovery at the chain.
-- INDUSTRY SEEKS REFUNDS FOR AXED PFI PROJECTS

The troubled Private Finance Initiative introduced by the Tory government could cost the taxpayer millions of pounds if contractors and banks proceed with claims for reimbursement for their costs in tendering for projects which have subsequently been withdrawn. The possibility of reimbursement comes ahead of an expected announcement by the Department of Health that 43 planned hospital projects are to be cut to perhaps six.
-- RESCUE OF CREDIT LYONNAIS COULD COST STATE 17 BILLION STG

French taxpayers could face a bill of almost 170 billion francs (17.74 billion stg) to rescue the state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais. The new figure, released in a draft report from the parliamentary committee set up to monitor the bank's restructuring, is substantially higher than previous estimates. The European Commission granted approval for state aid of 50 billion francs to the bank; the revised figure could see the Commission clash with France over the approval of further aid.
-- EMU SET TO FORCE CHANGE ON BASIC BANKING

A study from Salomon Brothers has claimed that European economic and monetary union (Emu) could accelerate the trend from bank deposits towards direct investment in securities. The paper, which looks at bank credit versus capital markets post Emu, suggests that a combination of new technology and Emu would take away the competitive advantage enjoyed in Europe by traditional commercial banking.
-- LEVY MAY FALL FOUL OF ENERGY TREATIES

A leading expert on international energy law has warned that the new Labour government's proposed 'windfall tax' on privatised utilities could face a serious legal challenge under international treaties. Professor Thomas Walde claims that an international tribunal could conclude that the levy amounts to 'creeping expropriation', and that it could also fall foul of the Energy Charter Treaty of 1994 which outlaws 'confiscatory taxation'. (Financial Times p. 13)
-- CENTRICA TO RENEGOTIATE DEALS

Centrica, the gas supply business demerged from British Gas GAS.L, has said it intends to settle almost one third of its so-called 'take-or-pay' long-term gas supply contracts with North Sea producers in time for the introduction of competition in the gas market in April 1998. The contracts commit Centrica to buying gas it no longer needs at a price well above market rates, and the group plans to renegotiate the terms of the contracts covering the purchase of some 25 billion therms - out of a total of 88 billion therms - over the next 12 months.
-- ALPHATEC CREDITORS EXPECTED TO CALL ON CHIEF TO GO

Charn Uswachoke, the chief executive of troubled Thai computer chip maker Alphatec Electronics, could be ousted from the company on Tuesday. Creditors of Alphatec are expected to call for his resignation before they agree to give the company time to restructure its overdue debts. Alphatec has faced a credit squeeze since US group Texas Instruments decided in May to pull out of projects worth $1.4 billion with the parent Alphatec Group.
-- REED TO PAY $447 MILLION FOR CHILTON TRADE TITLES

Anglo-Dutch media and information group Reed Elsevier is to acquire the three main trade press publishing divisions of US group Chilton for $447 million (270 million stg). The move is part of Reed's strategy of expansion into professional 'must have' information, and follows the purchase three months ago of US business MDL Information Systems for $320 million.
